Chapter 10. The Invitation—Faith in a Skeptical Age.
At the end of the day, those big questions—they’re still with us, aren’t they? Is there really a God? Does this life actually mean something? Can love and justice ever truly win out? For so many of us, this journey just keeps unfolding. Sometimes we move forward, sometimes we take a step back.
Imagine a young professional, worn out by all the cynicism around her. She’s tried out skepticism, hoping it would fill that emptiness, but honestly—it just leaves her feeling hollow. One quiet evening, she lets herself wonder. What if there’s something more? What if, just maybe, that bigger story is real?
Most people don’t realize—faith isn’t about jumping blindly into the unknown. It’s more like taking a small step toward the light. It’s not about shutting down hard questions, but opening up to the idea that life might hold more than what we can see right in front of us.
There’s a man who’s spent years searching, and to his surprise, he stumbles into joy. Not because his doubts have vanished, but because hope shows up in the middle of it all. He learns that faith isn’t about having everything figured out. It’s about trust—a willingness to believe that love is real, that forgiveness can actually happen, that our lives carry meaning no matter what.
The more you look at it, the more you see—the invitation of faith isn’t about running away from the world. It’s about stepping into it, fully engaged. It means caring about justice, chasing after truth, loving people even when it’s tough. The story isn’t about dodging pain, it’s about discovering hope right in the middle of it.
So, here’s the invitation for all of us living in a skeptical age: come and see. Bring your questions. Bring your doubts, your hopes, all of it. The journey isn’t always easy, but you don’t have to walk it alone.
